questions.prompt: Your first 6 replay trades were all losses. What is the most sensible view?

options.text: The rules are broken, so drop them now and start again with a different method
options.explanation: No: 6 trades is a tiny sample. Losing streaks happen even with sound rules.

options.text: Too early to judge; check you followed the plan and keep collecting trades
options.explanation: Right: a small sample says little.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of look-ahead bias?

options.text: Drawing support on a past chart using a low that formed after your entry
options.explanation: Right: you used information that did not exist at the time.

options.text: Testing on a quiet, ranging period you chose in advance
options.explanation: No: no future information is used. Picking periods before you look, including quiet ones, is a good way to reduce selection bias.

questions.prompt: You only test periods you remember as big trends. What bias is this?

options.explanation: No: look-ahead bias is using future information.
Right: this is selection bias, also called cherry-picking. You only test what stood out, and leave out the rest.
No: survivorship bias is copying a method because it is one of the ones that happened to work. Picking only the periods you remember is selection bias.

questions.prompt: You add a filter that removes 5 past losers. How do you know if it helps?

options.text: The past results improved, so it helps
options.explanation: No: it was chosen from those trades. That is overfitting.

options.text: Test it as a new plan version on fresh periods
options.explanation: Right: only new data can show that.

questions.prompt: Fictional test: 40 trades, 12 wins of +3R, 28 losses of −1R. Net result?
What can a 50-trade replay test show you?

options.text: Whether the plan has a real edge that will keep working on a live account in future
options.explanation: No: past tests promise nothing about the future.

options.text: How your rules behave in different conditions and how well you follow them
options.explanation: Right: it is a learning tool, not a forecast.
